rationale: Record a bound on the removed-leader finding that came out of attempting the lease-based route: Config validation forces CheckQuorum when ReadOnlyLeaseBased is selected, and with CheckQuorum the remaining voters refuse vote requests while they still hear the removed leader inside their election-timeout lease, so a new leader cannot be elected and nothing newer is committed while the removed leader serves its lease-based reads. The draft scenario confirms the mechanism natively (the campaign for node 2 did not win while node 3's lease held and its read was the only one answered, at an index nothing newer exceeded), so the lease-based configuration is excluded from the defect rather than another instance of it. The question's discriminator drops that item; the forwarded-route and PreVote items stay.

knowledge.statement: ReadOnlyLeaseBased cannot be combined with CheckQuorum disabled (Config.validate rejects it), and with CheckQuorum enabled a voter inside its election-timeout lease ignores a vote request from a higher term, so while the remaining voters still hear a leader they will not elect another one; a removed leader that keeps being answered therefore keeps a live lease rather than serving stale lease-based reads, and when the voters stop answering, its own quorum check fails and it steps down.
knowledge.conditions: Cluster whose remaining voters still answer the removed leader's heartbeats; ReadOnlyLeaseBased with CheckQuorum enabled (the only accepted combination).

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same missing membership check produces a stale answer through a route that was not exercised - a forwarded MsgReadIndex answered with MsgReadIndexResp - and whether PreVote combined with CheckQuorum changes the measured one-heartbeat bound.

interpretations.rationale: The measured account of this question is unchanged and rests on receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45: the removed leader answers a read immediately with an index below the entry the actual leader had already committed (parsed index 14), the actual leader's own answer covers its commit index, and the exposure ends when the removed leader steps down one heartbeat interval after the new leader is elected (indices 15 and 16) because the current leader answers the old-term heartbeat with its higher term. What this update adds is a bound discovered while attempting the lease-based route named in the question's discriminator. Config.validate rejects ReadOnlyLeaseBased unless CheckQuorum is enabled (raft.go:233-244), and with CheckQuorum a voter inside its election-timeout lease ignores a vote request carrying a higher term (raft.go:1100-1112). The draft scenario set up the same removal in a three-voter cluster with ReadOnlyLeaseBased and CheckQuorum and then campaigned the remaining voter: node 2 reached only StateCandidate at term 2 with its commit index still at 2, because node 3 kept its lease while it still heard the removed leader; the removed leader's own read was answered at index 2, which nothing newer exceeded, and the control read on node 2 was not answered at all because node 2 never became leader. That is the negative result: in this configuration the removed leader is still the leader the remaining voters acknowledge, so its lease-based answers are not stale, and if those voters stop answering, its own quorum check fails and it steps down. The lease-based route is therefore excluded from the defect rather than an extension of it - the stale-read exposure needs CheckQuorum to be off, which is incompatible with lease-based reads - and the question's discriminator now lists only the forwarded-route and PreVote items. The native scenario is not a retained receipt and the control read in it is incomplete (node 2 never led), so nothing in this update is claimed as a completed comparison; the bound is recorded as a source-explained negative with its supporting native observation.
counterevidence: The measured witness itself is unchanged and remains supported by the receipt cited above, including its controls (the actual leader answers correctly) and its measured step-down bound.

The lease-based configuration does not reproduce the stale answer: it requires CheckQuorum, whose lease makes the remaining voters refuse to elect a new leader while they still hear the removed leader, so nothing newer is committed while its lease-based answers are served.

The native lease-based scenario is incomplete as evidence: the campaigning node never became leader, so its control read was not answered and the observation only shows the mechanism (a vote ignored inside the lease), not a stale read.
limitations: The scenario requires the application to apply a committed change that removes the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; applications that set that option, or that stop the removed node, do not reach it.

The witness is at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipt shows the returned index is below an already-committed entry and that no confirmation message was sent. No state machine was run, so the miss of that write in a served value is a consequence of the contract, not something the receipt measures.
The measured bound is one heartbeat interval in the exercised configuration (one heartbeat tick, election timeout ten); other tick ratios and PreVote combined with CheckQuorum are not measured.

The forwarded route (a follower's MsgReadIndex answered with MsgReadIndexResp) is not exercised, and the source reason that no stale outcome was constructed for it in the single-voter shape is unchanged.
The lease-based negative is supported by source reading plus an incomplete native scenario (the campaign did not produce a leader), not by a retained receipt.

knowledge.assertion: IsSingleton is a size-only test over the configuration and never compares the single voter with the local node.
StepLeader answers MsgReadIndex locally whenever IsSingleton holds, using its own commit index and without a round.
A removed leader keeps leading by default while its proposals are refused and its read answers are not.
Lease-based reads force CheckQuorum, and the lease makes voters refuse higher-term vote requests while they still hear the leader.
